summary.intent: Work through the NEXT-WORK.md plan for the callisto release tool: start parallel lanes (cleanup/docs, SYS-RETRY, init.rs refactor, SYS-NAPI, derive.rs split) and then keep going through the hardening and T06 canonical-identity backlog until done.
summary.outcome: Opened a large set of PRs (#202-#208 and roughly a dozen more through #272 and beyond) covering the SYS-RETRY fix, mixed-routing test, docs refresh, init.rs/template refactors, SYS-NAPI, derive.rs split, CI hygiene, E317/E318/E319 errors, pre-mode no-repeat bump, dist-tag/snapshot refusal, canonical ecosystem/name emission, edition 2024, fuzz targets and unwrap denial. Each was gated by local `just ci`; the final panic-hygiene CI rerun was still in progress. Closed PR #201 after the user said the plan file must stay local.

repo: Plan/tracking files such as NEXT-WORK.md must stay local at .claude/plans/ (excluded via .git/info/exclude) and never go in a commit or PR.
Gate is `just ci`; the wrapper script's task-notification only reports the script exit, so the log's own `exit=` line must be read. Several runs showed exit=1 from fmt-check despite a wrapper exit 0.
Release tests rely on a fake publisher harness (release_harness.rs); fakes can hide real-tool bugs, so SYS-NAPI was proven with the real binary and real jq.
Existing tests assumed 'tag on HEAD means released', which was the SYS-RETRY defect; they had to tag an older commit instead.
Template constants for init now live in .tmpl files under crates/callisto-graph/src/templates/, with insta snapshots of rendered bytes guarding the move.
Generated workflow shell must be portable to macOS bash (no mapfile).
Intent omits artifactSlots when empty, so `.artifactSlots[]` iterates null in the template's jq.
Spec criteria in docs/specs/*.json, docs/errors.md (E317-E319 added) and a .changeset entry accompany each behavior change; breaking config changes need a minor bump.
Squash-merged branches make `git branch --merged` unreliable for cleanup; PRs are stacked with `gh stack` natively (#207 holds #205, #206, #208).
Commits are signed, PRs are opened ready-for-review, and no session link goes in commits or PRs per AGENTS.md.

code.finding: Roster derivation gained a 'resumable' set so packages tagged at HEAD are observed across all operations and stay selected until satisfied.
Tag peeling originally compared annotation text and errored on multi-paragraph tag messages; fixed to read only the object type.
The large derive function was split into stage functions with characterization snapshots first; uploads_by_package moved into OpIndex to satisfy clippy.
After E317, the second bare pass, promoted_siblings and bare-rule diagnostic emission are unreachable and were removed in a follow-up PR.

workflow: Write the failing reproduction first, then verify with mutation tests (revert/mutate source and confirm the test fails).
Scripted bulk edits (qualify.py/fixup.py) can silently alter unrelated comments; review the staged diff before committing.

The sandbox rejects inline env commands, heredocs, and some git-mentioning inline scripts and only allows edits inside the current worktree, so scripts were written to temp files and worktrees were switched.
Background sessions cannot edit the shared checkout, so the local plan file could not be updated from within worktrees.
An independent review agent was used on the riskiest PR (#202) and produced findings that were then fixed.
Escaped backticks in a quoted heredoc leave literal backslashes in PR bodies; use a body file instead.

friction: Opened PR #201 containing a local-only plan file; the user objected and it had to be closed.
The plan path in the initial lane summary was wrong.
Sandbox restrictions on inline commands and cross-worktree edits forced many workarounds.
CI wrapper exit codes misleadingly showed 0 when the log showed failures (fmt-check), several times.
rg -E flag error dropped build output once, and a sed one-liner failed on macOS.
The scripted conversion double-prefixed ecosystems and corrupted a colon-form test input and two comments.
Initial coarse fixes and fake tools had hidden bugs, per the saved feedback memory.

#204 still lists SYS-RETRY/T08-RETRY and needs a follow-up edit once #202 merges.
